clue.text: One on the beat, say, makes a good conductor

definitions.meaning: a police officer walking a beat, slangily a cop
the red metal carries electricity and heat very well

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a policeman on patrol, and also a metal prized for conducting electricity.

clue.text: Deliberate demolition of cottage I admitted

indicators.note: the single letter is let inside the rearranged letters
the cottage is knocked down and its letters rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: A purposeful knocking down of a cottage, which the speaker confesses to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolition of' rearranges COTTAGE; 'admitted' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to ponder or think something over carefully.

clue.text: Rendered incapable through drink

definitions.meaning: coated with a layer of plaster, as a wall is rendered

explanation.definitionFit: A wall rendered has been coated in plaster; and slang for very drunk.

clue.text: It's wrong to be stuck up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is put upwards, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: A moral remark that being snobbish is a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck up' looks like snobbery; in a down clue it turns LIVE upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness, moral wrongdoing.

clue.text: What's missing in a fight is obscure

indicators.note: the missing thing is placed within the word for a fight

parts.note: a bout is a boxing contest or fight
a lack is something absent or wanting

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is lacking in a boxing match and finds it unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: To black out a window or text is to darken it so it cannot be seen, i.e. obscure it.

clue.text: Enthusiasts may wax it

parts.note: suggests polishing, but recalls the idiom of speaking with great enthusiasm

explanation.definitionFit: To wax poetic about something is to talk about it with gushing enthusiasm.

clue.text: Catch the boss in a boiled shirt?

parts.note: to collar someone is to catch them
a stud is a boss, a raised knob

explanation.surface: Grabbing the manager in his stiff formal shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: A boiled shirt is an old-fashioned starched dress shirt, whose detachable collar is fixed with this small fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A small button-like fastener holding a detachable collar on a starched formal shirt.

clue.text: Surpass all others as a swindler

definitions.meaning: a swindler will do people out of their money

explanation.definitionFit: To beat everyone else, and also how a cheat would do someone out of their cash.

clue.text: Lay on a party

definitions.meaning: to lay on is to beat or attack
British slang for a lively party

explanation.definitionFit: To beat soundly, and a slang term for a big celebration.

clue.text: Main way to fasten sheets together

definitions.meaning: a bent wire clip driven through papers

explanation.definitionFit: Principal or basic, and a wire clip for joining papers.

clue.text: A dog trial produces a champion

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are worked up into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A canine competition turns out a winning hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' rearranges the nine letters of A DOG TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman arena fighter, and by extension anyone who fights for a cause, a champion.

clue.text: Alert for a change in the future

indicators.note: the letters are altered in order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Advice to stay watchful from now on, by way of variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done afterwards, at a subsequent time, happens in the future.

clue.text: What the ballerina wore for the African bishop

definitions.meaning: the short stiff skirt of a ballet dancer

explanation.definitionFit: A dancer's frilly skirt, and the surname of the famous South African churchman Desmond.

clue.text: They watch sport etc as recreation

indicators.note: read as re-creation: the letters are made again in a new order

explanation.surface: People watching sporting events as a leisure pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreation' (read as re-creation) rearranges SPORT ETC AS.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience at a match are onlookers, people who watch.

clue.text: Game in which Tom goes nap

definitions.text: Game in which Tom goes nap

parts.words: Game in which Tom goes nap
parts.note: nap suggests a card game, but means the tomcat has a sleep in its bed

explanation.definitionFit: A string-figure game whose name pictures a sleeping cat's bed.

clue.text: Two sailors start eating — sauce required

parts.note: a tar is a sailor; two of them give the word twice
the second sailor, another tar

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word eating is used

explanation.surface: A pair of seamen begin their meal and ask for a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold mayonnaise-based condiment with capers and gherkins, served with fish.

clue.text: The boy found embracing the girl is beaten

indicators.note: the boy's word wraps round the girl's word as in a hug

parts.note: a lad is a boy
she is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: A lad caught hugging a girl gets a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipped or flogged, so struck repeatedly: beaten.

clue.text: Dine out on hot food when up in northern capital

indicators.note: the letters of dine are put out of order
in a down clue the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: Eating out on a hot meal while visiting a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DINE to EDIN; 'when up' turns H GRUB upwards to BURGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Scotland, in the north of Britain.

clue.text: They do well out of those who fail oral examinations

definitions.text: They do well out of those who fail oral examinations

parts.words: They do well out of those who fail oral examinations
parts.note: suggests examiners profiting from failed students, but means mouth checkups that find decay

explanation.definitionFit: Tooth doctors earn fees treating patients whose mouth checkups reveal problems.

clue.text: A famous man, but there's no airs about him

indicators.note: the phrase is turned around and read from its end

parts.note: taken as written
side means pretentious airs, as in putting on side

explanation.surface: Praise for a celebrity who is quite unpretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole phrase round. 'Side' is old British slang for pretentious airs, as in 'putting on side'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, the American inventor of the phonograph, is a celebrated figure.

clue.text: Failure of phone or exchange

indicators.note: the letters swap places, as in a telephone exchange

explanation.surface: A breakdown at the telephone exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no chance of success is a failure.

clue.text: Rake money in, in the usual way

indicators.note: the money word is set inside the rake word

parts.note: a roue is a rake, a dissolute man
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Gathering in cash as one normally does.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first 'in' signals the container; the second is a link word. Tin as slang for money is old British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed regular procedure is the customary way of doing things.

clue.text: Change roles?

parts.note: suggests swapping jobs, but means allocating a play's parts to different actors

explanation.definitionFit: To give a play's parts to new actors, or to reshape something.

clue.text: Fighting observed in the capital

parts.note: war is fighting
saw means observed

explanation.surface: Combat seen in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Poland.

clue.text: Dessert wine may give one a minor jolt

parts.note: afters is British informal for the pudding course
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: Pudding wine might give a person a little jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British slang for dessert; HOCK is a German white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A smaller tremor following an earthquake is a lesser jolt.

clue.text: General course for a singer

definitions.meaning: the overall drift or gist of something

explanation.definitionFit: The gist of an argument, and a high male voice in a choir.

clue.text: Egg on a steak, say

parts.note: steak sounds like stake, and a stake is a bet

explanation.surface: A fried egg served on top of a steak, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' looks like a breakfast; it is the verb meaning urge. 'steak, say' is stake, which means a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge or encourage someone, especially to wrongdoing, is to egg them on.

clue.text: A conservative leader about to give ground

indicators.note: the front letter of conservative is taken

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A Tory chief is set to cede territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land area, so a measure of ground.

clue.text: Church council saying evil is peculiar?

indicators.note: the words are spoken aloud and give a sound-alike

parts.note: evil is sin, peculiar is odd: sin odd

explanation.surface: A church assembly declaring wickedness strange.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN (evil) and ODD (peculiar) spoken together sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly of clergy and church members governing a church.

clue.text: One-sided views we may get from people on holiday

definitions.text: One-sided views we may get from people on holiday

parts.words: One-sided views we may get from people on holiday
parts.note: sounds like biased opinions, but means pictures printed on one face of cards mailed home by travellers

explanation.definitionFit: Cards mailed by travellers have a picture on one side only, a one-sided view.

clue.text: Wanting to rest in peace?

parts.note: suggests the dead, but means tired of fighting and longing for peace

explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted by conflict and longing for peacetime.

clue.text: Man is in trouble — gets engaged

indicators.note: the man word sits within the trouble word

parts.note: a mess is a difficult situation, trouble
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man in difficulties becomes betrothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear teeth that interlock are said to engage.
